theme.title: The Cow Palace sweep
theme.subtitle: Golden State, 1974–75
theme.recap: The Warriors defeated the favored Bullets by winning close games behind Rick Barry, a deep bench and a relentless second-half defense.

questions.prompt: How many regular-season games did the 1974–75 Warriors win?
questions.note: 48 wins, before the Warriors took the title.

funFacts.text: The Bullets entered the Finals with far more regular-season wins than Golden State.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Golden State Warriors (48–34) played against the Eastern Conference champion Washington Bullets (60–22)

funFacts.text: The championship was Golden State's first since 1956, when the franchise played in Philadelphia.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: win their first championship since 1956, when the team was still based in Philadelphia

funFacts.text: Golden State traded future Hall of Famer Nate Thurmond to Chicago for young center Clifford Ray before the season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they traded future Hall of Famer Nate Thurmond to the Chicago Bulls for young center Clifford Ray

questions.prompt: How many points did Rick Barry score in Game 2 of the 1975 Finals?
questions.context: Golden State vs Washington · 1975 Finals · Game 2
questions.note: 36 points in a one-point Warriors win.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: led by 36 points from Rick Barry

funFacts.text: The Warriors had to play their home Finals games at the Cow Palace because Oakland Arena was booked for the Ice Follies.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Oakland facility being unavailable due to the Ice Follies

funFacts.text: Washington got a final chance in Game 2 with six seconds remaining but missed both shots.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Washington got the ball back with six seconds left but missed two shots

funFacts.text: Barry had previously played for the rival ABA before returning to the Warriors.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: briefly lost Rick Barry to the American Basketball Association

questions.prompt: How many points ahead were the Bullets at halftime of Game 1 of the 1975 Finals?
questions.context: Washington Bullets vs Golden State · Game 1
questions.note: 14 points, before Golden State's second-half comeback.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Bullets built a 14-point lead at the half over the Warriors

funFacts.text: Warriors reserve Phil Smith provided an unexpected scoring boost off the bench during the comeback.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Phil Smith coming off the bench to score 20 points in 31 minutes

funFacts.text: The opening game took place at the Capital Centre in Landover, Maryland, outside Washington.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Capital Centre, Landover, Maryland

funFacts.text: Golden State reached the Finals after defeating the Chicago Bulls in a seven-game Western final.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: then eliminated Thurmond and the Bulls in seven games to advance to the Finals

questions.prompt: How many rebounds did Wes Unseld grab in Game 2 of the 1975 Finals?
questions.context: Washington Bullets at Golden State · 1975 Finals
questions.note: 20 rebounds, but Washington lost the game by a single point.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Rebs: Wes Unseld 20

funFacts.text: Jamaal Wilkes's undersized but effective defense on Elvin Hayes proved decisive.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the defensive play of the seemingly undersized Jamaal Wilkes on Bullets' power forward Elvin Hayes

funFacts.text: Reserve center George Johnson added 10 points and nine rebounds in Game 3.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: backup center George Johnson had 10 points and nine rebounds off the bench

funFacts.text: Rick Barry had 38 points in Game 3 as the Warriors moved within a win of the title.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Rick Barry poured in 38 points

questions.prompt: How many points did Golden State score in Game 4 to clinch the 1975 Finals?
questions.note: 96 points, one more than Washington in the title clincher.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Golden State Warriors 96, Washington Bullets 95

funFacts.text: Coach Al Attles was ejected after a confrontation with Mike Riordan, leaving assistant Joe Roberts to finish the game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Attles bolted onto the court and initiated a fight of his own with Riordan

funFacts.text: The 1975 Finals are the oldest NBA championship series with full television coverage still surviving.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The 1975 Finals is also the oldest NBA championship series whose TV coverage still exists in its entirety

funFacts.text: Rick Barry went on to work as a broadcaster for the next six NBA Finals, including while still an active player.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Barry went on to cover the next six NBA Finals, five of which while still an active player
